subGaps.description: zeros data blocker: resolved — zeros6 combined file (2M zeros, ~35 MB) downloaded to scripts/.zeros-cache/zeros6 on 2026-04-12. ZEROS_EXTENDED in zeros-to-1e6.js still has 100K entries; updating it to 1M+ is deferred pending imp514b/d resolution.

compute feasibility: Float64 RK4 in Node.js handles N up to ~250K-400K (minutes to hours). N=600K-1M requires C/Rust backend (Arb, CAPD, or custom). This script cannot fully close imp-514 for N=1M without native code.

certification: Float64 RK4 gives t_c central value without error bars. Interval arithmetic (interval-dyson-integrator.mjs) is certified but returns budget-exhausted for N>100K. Closing imp-514 with certified bounds at N=1M requires a native Arb/CAPD backend.

step-size overshoot at large N: for N >= 150K the initial minimum gap between adjacent Riemann zeros can be smaller than 2*sqrt(dt). The Dyson nearest-pair collapse time T~gap^2/4 is then less than dt, so the first RK4 step overshoots the collision and reports a spurious t_c~dt. N=150K run produced t_c=0.0001 vs OLS=0.00668 (67x discrepancy). Row flagged source=suspect-overshoot-artifact and excluded from cache overrides. Resolution: seed dt from initial minimum gap or use native C/Rust backend.

usageNote: Import these rows into dyson-ladder-measured.js to replace PROJECTED_ROWS at matching N. Only rows with source="measured-float64-rk4" and reason="gap-nonpositive" carry a meaningful collision time. Rows with source="suspect-overshoot-artifact" are excluded from overrides. Budget-exhausted rows report t_c as a lower bound.
